196: Rabbi Yitzchak said, there are three matters here: A sigh, a groan, a scream. Each one is distinct from the other. A sigh: as it says, "and the children of Israel sighed." A scream: As it says, "and they screamed." A groan: As it says, "and their groaning rose up." Each one is distinct, and Israel did each of these. Rabbi Yehudah said, they screamed and they groaned, but they did not sigh. This is implied by what is written, "וַיֵּאָנְחוּ - and they were sighed", and the sigh was on their behalf on High.
